reason: I’ll fit the salivary glands to begin assembling the digestive system; their ducts lead into the mouth.
expectation: The glands will attach to the digestive tube, leaving the other slots to fill.

alternatives.reason: Starting starch digestion also seems useful, but I’d like to assemble the organs first.

effect: The salivary glands are fitted, so I can continue assembling the digestive organs.
reaction: The attachment was straightforward; the picture did not add much about the glands’ function.
reason: The pancreas has a duct leading to the small intestine, so I’ll fit it next.
expectation: The pancreas will attach to the digestive tube, leaving the other slots available.

alternatives.reason: The liver and gallbladder also connect to the tube, but I chose the pancreas first.

effect: The pancreas is fitted, leaving the liver and gallbladder as the next available organ attachment.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though it added no explanation of the pancreas’s role.
reason: I’ll continue assembling the digestive system by connecting the liver and gallbladder.
expectation: The liver and gallbladder will fit into the digestive tube; the portal vessel slot may still remain.

alternatives.reason: Starting starch digestion is also useful, but I want to finish the available organ fittings first.

effect: The organ-fitting goal is complete, and the explanation connects each organ to digestion. I can now work on breaking down the meal.
reaction: The explanation made the earlier fittings more meaningful.
reason: I’ll start with starch and salivary amylase, following digestion from the mouth.
expectation: Amylase will break the starch into smaller carbohydrates, perhaps requiring further digestion.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the goal, but I chose to start with starch.

effect: Salivary amylase produced shorter starch chains, so further digestion appears necessary.
reaction: The result matched my expectation, though it added little explanation.
reason: I’ll continue breaking down the starch with the remaining digestive enzymes.
expectation: The enzymes will break the chains into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the goal, but I want to finish the starch pathway first.

effect: The starch pathway produced individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining. I can now break down the other foods.
reaction: The result clearly connected digestion to absorption.
reason: I’ll digest the protein next to continue preparing the meal for absorption.
expectation: The enzymes will break the protein into smaller components, possibly amino acids.

alternatives.reason: Fat digestion also advances the goal, but I chose protein first.

effect: Protein digestion produced amino acids, leaving fat digestion as the only offered combination.
reaction: The result was clear and matched my expectation, though it added no explanation.
reason: I’ll use the only available combination to break down the fat.
expectation: Bile and lipase will help break the fat into smaller components that can be absorbed.

effect: Fat digestion produced fatty acids and monoglycerides and completed the chapter. The explanation clarified that bile disperses fat while lipase breaks it apart.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing the organ fittings was worthwhile because the explanation connected the glands, pancreas and liver to their digestive roles.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pancreas felt repetitive on its own because the result gave no immediate explanation of its role.

surprise.text: The fat result clarified that bile disperses fat into droplets but is not an enzyme; lipase breaks the fat molecules apart.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt arbitrary: the organ slots and food-and-enzyme pairings gave them clear purposes, although the compatible menu supplied the pairings.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the products cross the intestinal lining, though the repeated fittings and simple combinations make me only moderately interested.
